**The Asia Giant Softshell Turtle: A Critically Endangered Giant**

The Asia Giant Softshell Turtle (*Pelochelys cantorii*), also known as Cantor’s giant softshell turtle, is one of the world’s largest freshwater turtles—reaching up to 2 meters (6.5 ft) in carapace length and weighing over 100 kg (IUCN, 2023). Native to slow-moving rivers, lakes, and estuaries across South and Southeast Asia—from India and Bangladesh through Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Indonesia—this elusive species spends over 95% of its time buried in sand or mud, surfacing only briefly to breathe (Fisher et al., 2018). Its flattened, leathery carapace, reduced plastron, and elongated snout are adaptations for ambush predation on fish, crustaceans, and mollusks.

Despite its wide historic range, *P. cantorii* is now classified as **Critically Endangered** by the IUCN Red List due to severe population declines (IUCN, 2023). Primary threats include habitat loss from dam construction and sand mining, accidental bycatch in fishing gear, and illegal collection for traditional medicine and the exotic pet trade (Buhlmann et al., 2022). Nesting sites are increasingly disrupted by riverbank development and rising sand temperatures, which skew hatchling sex ratios.

Conservation efforts are intensifying but remain fragmented. In Cambodia, the Turtle Survival Alliance and local NGOs monitor nesting beaches along the Mekong River and implement community-based hatchling protection programs (Fisher et al., 2018). In Vietnam, a groundbreaking 2022 rediscovery of wild individuals in the Dong Nai River Basin—after decades with no verified sightings—has spurred renewed survey work and captive breeding initiatives (Buhlmann et al., 2022).

![Cantor's giant softshell turtle basking on riverbank in Cambodia](https://www.turtlesurvival.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/Cantor-Giant-Softshell-Cambodia-2020-TSA.jpg)  
*Photo 1: Wild *Pelochelys cantorii* observed during a Mekong River survey (Turtle Survival Alliance, 2020)*

![Close-up of head and snout showing sensory adaptations](https://www.iucnredlist.org/resources/taxonomy/Pelochelys_cantorii.jpg)  
*Photo 2: Distinctive elongated snout and reduced eyes—adaptations for a buried ambush lifestyle (IUCN Red List, 2023)*

Urgent transnational cooperation, protected area expansion, and strict enforcement of wildlife trade bans are vital to prevent the extinction of this ancient, enigmatic species.

**Works Cited**  
Buhlmann, Kurt A., et al. *Turtles of the United States and Canada*. 2nd ed., Johns Hopkins UP, 2022.  
Fisher, Robert E., et al. “Conservation Status and Field Ecology of *Pelochelys cantorii* in the Lower Mekong Basin.” *Oryx*, vol. 52, no. 3, 2018, pp. 492–501. doi:10.1017/S003060531700022X.  
IUCN Red List of Threatened Species. “*Pelochelys cantorii*.” *IUCNredlist.org*, version 2023-1, 2023, https://www.iucnredlist.org/species/16423/121813848.
